title: Oxidation and Reduction Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
An iron gate turns brown, a cut apple browns on the plate, a gas flame burns blue. In this animated lesson that opens Class 11 Chemistry Chapter 7 (NCERT, Redox Reactions) Aarav finds rust on his bicycle chain and we ask what the iron really lost.

You will see the classical meaning first (oxidation adds oxygen or removes hydrogen, reduction does the opposite) with magnesium, hydrogen sulphide and copper oxide. Then on the molecule bench a zinc rod dips into blue copper sulphate: each zinc atom hands two electrons to a copper ion, copper coats the rod and the blue fades, with a live electron balance. We define oxidation as loss and reduction as gain of electrons (OIL RIG), write the two half reactions, compare the reducing agent and the oxidising agent, work through sodium and chlorine, show the agent trap, then an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 71 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Rust, browning, burning: one hidden swap
0:27 The old idea: oxygen and hydrogen
1:09 Zinc in copper sulphate on the molecule bench
1:38 Oxidation is loss, reduction is gain
1:54 Writing the two half reactions
2:17 OIL RIG
2:36 Reducing agent vs oxidising agent
3:14 Worked example: sodium and chlorine
3:50 Exam trap: which agent is reduced?
4:14 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:48 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Oxidation Number. How do we track electrons when nobody gives them away fully?
